title: The Japanese singer's tour offer to the Walton-Higgins trio
summary: Sam, Cedar Walton and Billy Higgins are invited to Japan by a pop singer, and record there with Sadao Watanabe and Hisao Suzuki.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah, uhm but uhm like I said after free lancing around New York here uhm, through the years, me and Walton and Billy Higgins became a rhythm section, and we start playing together different places. Traveling together, we was playing in one of those clubs, the man who own The Angry Squire, , he had another club on 23rd Street right off 10th Avenue, uh, we were in there playing. So a group of Japanese people came in there and uhm sit down, and they was, listened to us all night, and they came back the next night.
Uh huh.
But we didn't know this, this was one of the
leaders, one of the leading Japanese pop singers and uh, Japanese pop singers in Japan.
Uh huh.
So, so intermission she came up to, and said uh, she sure would like to take us to Japan to play for her on a tour.
That's so.

We thought this was another one of those dizzy broads, man, just, uh man, get out of here with that stuff, you know that's crazy. If you want to meet us, just say hello and go back to your seat and sit down. You know.
Right.

So, she said 'no, no, no, really see, this is my agent here,' there were some Japanese people and the man came up and said, 'we would like, see if this trio, we come, we, we, we have heard you all play.' and we can't believe it you know, we love this music. 'We wish that you could come to Japan and play.'
Uh huh.

So Cedar said 'well, let's talk about it.' So uh, come, so uh, we come back on stage and Cedar say 'hey man, you know what?' he said. 'We got a gig to go to Japan!' I said 'you're kidding me?' He said 'no, I'm not kidding. We're going to Japan man, and play for that lady on tour.' I said 'sure enough?' He said yeah.
HA HA HA.

And sure enough man, uh we went to Japan and played the first part of the concert with the trio, played for her, all th, all over the country, man, in Japan and without rhythm section a lot of Japanese musicians, you know, made records with us.
Oh yeah.
Over there, we recorded with what's his name, Sa...
Sadao Watanabe?

Sada. Made a record with him, made a record with uh, uh, Billy Higgins and I made records with a piano, a couple piano players over there and there's a bass player over there named Suzuki, Hisao Suzuki. He had a band so he played the uh cello.
Uh huh.
And I played the bass, he used our rhythm section we we made this million, all kinds of records over there, you know.
Uh huh.
And so on, on this tour , the man that set up this tour called. music, one of the biggest companies they bring all the big acts over there.
Uh huh.
